purpose: Held-out test of what each search method delivers: does surrogate-assisted LHFiD find better deployable configurations, not only a higher calibration hypervolume? Fixed before any C3 lock or run.
split: data/prompts/test2.json (500 COCO prompts, selection seed 20261116, image- and caption-disjoint from calibration, hold-out, validation and test)
lock_rule: scripts/lock_nas_finalists.py per arm with --max-finalists 5: pool all candidates of that arm, normalize latency by each job's reference, merge identical signatures, keep CLIP >= calibration reference - 1.0, fidelity >= 75, black <= reference + 2, take the 4-objective front, pick the best point on each objective then farthest-point fill
runs: every locked configuration (duplicates across arms run once and count for each arm) plus the 20-step DDIM reference at the start, middle and end; one allocation; 10 warm-ups; seeded shuffled order
primary_indicator: 4-D hypervolume of each arm's locked set on test2: CLIP (max), fidelity to the test2 reference (max), p50 latency (min), U-Net MB (min); reference point CLIP = test2 reference CLIP - 1.0, fidelity 75, 600 ms, 1,700 MB
primary_test: paired prompt bootstrap (10,000 resamples of prompts, seed 0) of HV(sa_lhfid) - HV(other) for each other arm; two-sided bootstrap p; Holm over the three comparisons
claim_rule: sa_lhfid's locked set is claimed better than an arm's if the Holm-adjusted p < 0.05 and the median bootstrap difference is positive
secondary: per configuration: CLIP non-inferiority vs the reference (margin 0.5, Holm within each arm), fidelity, black images, latency, GFLOPs, peak VRAM, U-Net MB, KID/FID vs real COCO; descriptive
